title: Getting a Handle on Unmanaged Memory
problem: Heap objects in unmanaged languages like C/C++ cannot be relocated, causing severe memory fragmentation in performance-critical applications such as databases and web servers. Programmers must apply Herculean effort on a per-application basis to mitigate these issues.
motivation: Memory fragmentation degrades performance and memory efficiency in unmanaged languages while managed languages elegantly solve this through compacting garbage collection, creating a capability gap between language paradigms.
method: Alaska introduces handles—a level of indirection between pointers and heap objects—enabling transparent object movement. A compiler automatically transforms pointer-based code to handle-based code with optimizations to minimize indirection overhead. A codesigned runtime system manages handles and exposes an extensible service interface for implementing memory management features like defragmentation.
key_novelty: Using compiler-synthesized handle indirection as a drop-in replacement for malloc to transparently enable compacting garbage collection and heap object movement in unmanaged languages.
contributions: Alaska compiler that automatically transforms unmodified pointer-based C/C++ code to handle-based equivalents with optimization strategies
Runtime system managing handle indirection with extensible services for heap object movement
Heap defragmentation service eliminating fragmentation and reducing memory usage by up to 40% in Redis
Framework bridging memory management capabilities between managed and unmanaged language runtimes
limitations: Performance overhead characteristics and scalability limitations not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: transparent heap compaction for unmanaged languages
